steps.stem: The economist Shani wrote: "Whether the rise in sales in the last quarter marks the beginning of a recovery is still very much in doubt, all the more so in view of the other developments in the market. For the time being, it is no more than a first sign." Which of the following best expresses Shani's statement?
choices: Taking into account the other developments in the market, it is certain that the recovery that began in the last quarter will continue
It is doubtful whether the rise in sales in the last quarter reflects the present state of the market
The rise in sales is indeed only a first sign, but it is already clear that a recovery has begun
In view of the other developments in the market, there is reason to doubt whether the rise in sales is the beginning of a lasting recovery
explanation: Shani doubts whether the rise in sales is the beginning of a recovery, especially because of other developments in the market. (1) and (3) turn the doubt into certainty; (2) moves the doubt from what the rise will lead to onto what it shows about the present.

steps.stem: Sarit: "At the new restaurant, most diners come back, so I assume the food there is ____." Sarit's words are not logical, but they would have been logical had she said ____ instead of "so," ____ instead of ____. Which of the following best completes the text?
choices: disappointing / "therefore" / or "few diners fail to come back" / "most diners come back"
excellent / "even so" / or alternatively "not excellent" / "excellent"
disappointing / "even so" / or "excellent" / "disappointing"
mediocre / "and yet" / and also "quite good" / "mediocre"
explanation: "Most come back, so … disappointing" is illogical; it becomes logical with a concession ("even so") or with a verdict that fits the evidence ("excellent"). (1) swaps in a synonym and a paraphrase, which change nothing; (2) starts from a logical sentence; (4) requires both changes at once, which makes the sentence illogical again.

steps.stem: The following sentence, taken from an announcement about a scholarship, can be understood in two ways: "The scholarship will be awarded only to nursing students who work at the city hospital and residents of the northern district." Which of the following is not possible according to either of the two ways of understanding the sentence?
choices: Einat, who works at the city hospital but is not a nursing student and does not live in the northern district, was awarded the scholarship
Hagai, a resident of the northern district who is not a nursing student and does not work at the city hospital, was awarded the scholarship
Nurit, a nursing student who lives in the northern district but does not work at the city hospital, was awarded the scholarship
Yoram, a resident of the northern district who is not a nursing student and does not work at the city hospital, was not awarded the scholarship
explanation: Reading 1: nursing student + hospital + north; reading 2: (nursing student + hospital) or a resident of the north. Einat is not a nursing student and does not live in the north, so she fails both. Hagai and Nurit fit reading 2, and "only" never forces an award, so Yoram is always possible.

steps.stem: A researcher asked two groups of participants to fill in a long questionnaire. One group filled it in in a heated room, and the other in a room that was not heated. At the end, all the participants were asked to donate to a fund for the renovation of the neighborhood playground. The participants who had been in the heated room donated considerably more, and the researcher concluded that the warmth had improved their mood. Which of the following assumptions underlies the researcher's conclusion?
choices: People who are in a bad mood do not pay attention to the temperature of the room they are in
A person in a good mood donates more than a person whose mood is less good
People who sit in a heated room are more willing to support the renovation of playgrounds
The participants in the heated room filled in the questionnaire faster than the other participants
explanation: The researcher infers the mood from the donations, so he must assume that a better mood leads to larger donations. (3) merely restates the finding, and (1) and (4) do not connect the donations to mood at all.

steps.stem: Tzipi: "It will be hard for me to arrange this violin sonata for the piano, and to arrange it for the guitar will be even harder." Yigal: "It follows from what you say that you play the piano better than the guitar." Yigal's claim is based on the assumption that a musician who finds it easier to arrange a piece ____ plays instrument A better than instrument B.
choices: from instrument A for instrument C than from instrument A for instrument B
from instrument A for instrument C than from instrument B for instrument C
from instrument A for instrument B than from instrument B for instrument A
from instrument C for instrument A than from instrument C for instrument B
explanation: Tzipi finds violin → piano easier than violin → guitar, and Yigal concludes that she plays the piano better, so ease of arranging for an instrument must reflect command of it: from C (violin) for A (piano) rather than for B (guitar). The other choices put the instruments in the wrong roles.

steps.title: Understanding sentences - the toolkit
steps.intro: What makes a sentence hard, and what to do about it.

head: Difficulty
What to do
rows: Eliminate by structure first; the key expression decides the rest
Find what makes it (il)logical; test each swap
Turn one pair of negatives into a positive at a time
Write both readings ("and" can act as "or"); check each choice against both
Find the unstated link between what was said and the conclusion

tips: "Only" = who can be accepted - not who must be.
The skill runs through all of verbal: no understanding, no conclusions.

steps.stem: Researchers who studied the speech of villages in the Galilee in the 1950s found that older residents avoided many words that young people brought back from the cities. At first the researchers assumed that the older residents did not understand these words, but they later found that most of them understood the words well and even used them when speaking with outsiders. Which of the following conclusions is best supported by these findings?
choices: Most of the older residents did not understand the words that the young people brought from the cities
The young people stopped using the new words when they came back to the villages
The older residents avoided the new words mainly when speaking among themselves
The researchers' first assumption was correct with regard to only a few of the words
explanation: The older residents understood the words and used them with outsiders, so their avoidance was limited to talk among themselves (3). (1) contradicts the later finding; (2) and (4) are not supported (the finding was about most residents, not about some words).

steps.stem: Pnina told Hezi that it was strange that their neighbor, who owns a restaurant, never cooks at home. Hezi replied that the electrician in their building had been living with a broken kitchen lamp for two years. Hezi's reply suggests that in his opinion -
choices: the neighbor does not like the food served in his own restaurant
people often neglect at home the work that they do for others
the neighbor is less skilled than people think
the electrician and the neighbor are both too busy to look after their own homes
explanation: Hezi answers with another professional who does not do his own work at home: the thing is common, not strange (2). (4) adds a reason he does not give, and (1) and (3) are about the neighbor's restaurant, which the example does not touch.

steps.stem: A food factory used to check every crate that left its gates, and its inspectors found few defects. Later, to save money, the factory began to check only one crate in ten, and the number of defects found rose sharply. The factory's manager noted that during this period there had been no change in the workers, the machines or the raw materials. Which of the following can be inferred from the manager's remark?
choices: The rise in the number of defects found probably reflects a change in the checking itself
The workers became less careful once they knew that most crates would not be checked
Checking one crate in ten saves money without harming the quality of the products
The more crates are checked, the fewer defects there are
explanation: If nothing in production changed, the rise in defects found must come from the checking (1). (2) contradicts "no change in the workers", (3) is not addressed, and (4) turns one factory's experience into a rule.

steps.stem: Two researchers at an experimental farm are comparing twelve plots that were sprayed this year with twelve plots that were not. Yael says: "Not one of the unsprayed plots produced a larger crop than the weakest sprayed plot." If Yael is right, which of the following is necessarily true?
choices: Every sprayed plot produced a larger crop than every unsprayed plot
Most of the sprayed plots produced larger crops than most of the unsprayed plots
No sprayed plot produced a smaller crop than any unsprayed plot
The spraying increased the farm's total crop this year
explanation: Every unsprayed plot ≤ the weakest sprayed plot ≤ every sprayed plot (3). (1) and (2) require "larger", which fails if some crops were equal; (4) is a causal claim that does not follow.

steps.stem: Very few complaints by villagers against tax collectors have survived in the Ottoman archives of a certain district, although the archives contain thousands of other documents from the same years, including detailed tax lists. Some historians have concluded from this that the collectors in the district were unusually fair. Others point out that complaints were often made orally to local officials and were not necessarily recorded, and that recorded complaints may have been kept in archives that did not survive. Which of the following is not implied by the paragraph?
choices: The district's archives are not poor in documents from the period in question
Some historians regard the small number of complaints as evidence about the collectors' conduct
A villager could complain without leaving a written record
Most of the complaints that were written down were lost
explanation: The paragraph raises the loss of recorded complaints only as a possibility and says nothing about most of them (4). (1) follows from "thousands of other documents", (2) is the first view, and (3) is the oral-complaint point.

steps.stem: The following sentence appeared in a local newspaper: "The committee rejected the proposal of the teachers' representative from the northern district." Which of the following is not a possible way of understanding the sentence?
choices: The committee rejected a proposal made by the representative of the teachers of the northern district
The committee members from the northern district rejected the proposal of the teachers' representative
The committee rejected a proposal from the northern district that the teachers' representative had brought
The teachers' representative, who comes from the northern district, had his proposal rejected by the committee
explanation: "From the northern district" can describe the teachers, the representative or the proposal (1, 3, 4). It cannot describe the committee members who rejected it (2).

steps.stem: Dafna, who sings in a youth choir, told her parents: "At the end of the year the conductor said that only a little less than two thirds of us had made the progress he had hoped for." According to Dafna, what did the conductor's words imply about the singers in the choir?
choices: That a little more than a third of them had made less progress than he had hoped
That about two thirds of them had not made the progress he had hoped for
That most of them had made no progress at all
That a third of them should leave the choir
explanation: Those who met his hopes are a little under two thirds, so the rest - a little over a third - made less progress than he hoped (1). (2) takes the group he mentioned as the other group; (3) and (4) are not said.

steps.stem: A worker complained to a factory's maintenance manager that all the machines in the hall where he works had stopped at the same moment. The manager replied: "When the lights go out in every room of a house at once, nobody starts replacing bulbs." Which of the following expresses the same idea as the manager's reply?
choices: When a machine stops, first check whether the worker operated it properly
Old machines break down more often than new ones
A machine that stops once a week needs more attention than one that stops once a year
When all the children in a kindergarten fall ill in the same week, the doctor asks what they ate
explanation: A failure of everything at once points to one common cause; the doctor who looks for something all the children shared follows the same idea (4). (1), (2) and (3) are about single machines, age and frequency.

steps.stem: A clerk who copied numbers from old handwritten ledgers made three kinds of mistakes: sometimes he wrote a number twice; sometimes, when the same number appeared twice in succession, he wrote it only once; and sometimes he read a 7 as a 1, since the two looked alike in the original handwriting. An auditor who compared the ledgers with the copies found four discrepancies. Which of them cannot be explained by the clerk's three kinds of mistakes?
choices: The ledger shows 77 and the copy shows 17
The ledger shows 17 and the copy shows 71
The ledger shows 40, 12 and the copy shows 40, 40, 12
The ledger shows 12, 12, 9 and the copy shows 12, 9
explanation: (2) reverses the order of the digits, which is none of the three kinds. (1) reads the first 7 as a 1, (3) writes a number twice, and (4) writes once a number that appeared twice.

steps.stem: Under a village's bylaws, a request to add a floor to a house can be approved only if it is submitted by a member who has lived in the village for at least ten years, or jointly by two members who have lived there for a combined total of at least fifteen years. Which of the following requests can be approved under the bylaws?
choices: A request submitted jointly by a member who has lived in the village for nine years and his wife, also a member, who has lived there for five
A request by a member who moved to the village nine years ago, after living for twenty years in a neighboring village
A request submitted by the village council on behalf of a member who arrived two years ago
A request submitted jointly by two members who have each lived in the village for eight years
explanation: Eight plus eight is sixteen years combined (4). (1) totals fourteen, in (2) the twenty years were not in the village, and in (3) the request is not submitted by qualifying members.

steps.stem:
Nava: "When a child misbehaves, the first thing to do is to ask him why."
Tzvi: "Nonsense. First you tell him to stop; there will be time for questions afterwards."
Nava: "I did not say that the questions replace stopping him. Of course he has to stop - I only think that the question should come first."
Which of the following best describes the disagreement between Nava and Tzvi?
choices: They disagree about the order in which a parent should act, not about what the parent should eventually do
Nava thinks that the child's reasons matter more than stopping the behavior, whereas Tzvi thinks the opposite
Tzvi thinks that a child who misbehaves should not be asked for his reasons at all
They agree about everything, but Tzvi misunderstood Nava's first remark
explanation: Both want the child stopped and questioned; they differ only on what comes first (1). (2) and (3) contradict their words, and (4) ignores that they still disagree about the order.

steps.stem: The founder of a small theater told an interviewer that the newspapers had been wrong to describe the theater's first season as a failure. "The first performances sold out," he said. "Our problem was that people who had seen one play did not come to the next." Which of the following best summarizes the founder's claim?
choices: The newspapers exaggerated the number of empty seats at the theater's first performances, which were in fact well attended
The theater had no difficulty attracting an audience, but it did have difficulty keeping one
The first plays were poor, and most of the people who came to see them left disappointed
The theater's later plays were more successful than its first ones
explanation: Sold-out first performances, but people did not return (2). (1) is not claimed, (3) gives a reason he does not give, and (4) contradicts his description.

steps.stem: A notice at the entrance to a library reads: "Books may be borrowed for two weeks. Readers who return a book late will not be allowed to borrow more than one book at a time for a month." Which of the following is consistent with the notice?
choices: A reader who returned a book three days late borrowed one book a week later
A reader who returned a book late borrowed three books at once the following week
A reader kept a book for three weeks and was not restricted in any way afterwards
A reader who returned a book late borrowed two books at once three weeks later
explanation: After a late return the reader may borrow only one book at a time for a month; (1) keeps to this. (2) and (4) borrow several books within the month, and (3) kept the book late without the restriction that follows.

steps.stem: In an interview about his latest novel, a writer said: "This is the first book I have written that I would have shown my father without fear, had he still been alive." Which of the following can be inferred from the writer's words?
choices: The writer's father read only some of his son's books
The writer considers his latest novel his best book
There is at least one earlier book that the writer would have hesitated to show his father
The writer's father had disapproved of his son's decision to become a writer and rarely read his books
explanation: If this is the first book he would have shown without fear, then each earlier book he would have shown with fear - in particular at least one (3). (2) turns "without fear" into "best", and (1) and (4) say things about the father that are not said.

steps.stem: A historian who read some four hundred letters written by members of a family of grain merchants over three generations, between 1840 and 1910, found that nearly every letter mentions the current price of wheat, often in its first lines. None of the letters, however, explains why the price concerned the writers so much - even in years when, according to its account books, the family was not trading in wheat at all. Which of the following best summarizes the historian's findings?
choices: The family's interest in the price of wheat stemmed from its trade in wheat
Only some of the letters mention the price of wheat, mostly in years in which the family traded in it
The account books explain what the letters do not: why the family was so interested in the price of wheat
The letters show how much the price of wheat concerned the family, but not the reason for this concern
explanation: Nearly every letter mentions the price, none explains the concern (4). (1) is contradicted by the years without trade, (2) reverses "nearly every", and (3) credits the account books with an explanation they do not give.

steps.stem: At a council meeting, a member put a question to the head of the council and demanded a plain "yes" or "no". The head of the council refused, saying that even a person who had done nothing wrong could not answer it either way without incriminating himself. Which of the following questions could an innocent person answer with "yes" or "no" without incriminating himself?
choices: Did you know about the delay in building the new school before the newspapers reported it?
Have you stopped giving council contracts to your relatives?
Was it your deputy who advised you to hide the auditor's report from the council members?
Do you regret the building permits you granted in return for money to contractors who supported you in the election?
explanation: An innocent person can answer (1) either way. (2), (3) and (4) take a wrongdoing for granted, so both "yes" and "no" admit it - they could be the question that was asked.

steps.stem: This year a certain species of migrating bird arrived in Israel later than in previous years. Some attributed this to the cold winter that preceded the migration. A birdwatcher rejects this explanation: in his opinion, when there is an abundance of insects these birds arrive early, and therefore it is not reasonable that the cold winter is what delayed them. On which of the following assumptions does the birdwatcher rely?
choices: In a cold winter it is difficult for the birds to find insects along the migration route
In years in which the winter is warm, the birds arrive late
A cold winter brings about an abundance of insects
Last winter was not colder than previous winters, although many people felt that it was
explanation: The argument works only if a cold winter → many insects → early arrival, which clashes with the late arrival; the first link is unstated (3). (1) would support the cold-winter explanation; (2) and (4) are not needed.

steps.stem: A young writer complained to a friend: "I gave the editor two pages and a twenty-page story at the same time. He finished the story that evening, but kept the two pages for a week." Her friend replied: "That does not mean that he preferred the story." Which of the following, if true, best supports the friend's reply?
choices: The editor usually rejects short texts submitted by young writers
The editor believes that in a short text every word must be weighed carefully
Long stories are easier to write than short texts
The editor published the twenty-page story in the next issue of his journal
explanation: If short texts demand that every word be weighed, the week spent on two pages reflects care, not preference (2). (1) and (4) support the opposite, and (3) is about writing, not reading.

steps.stem: In an article on school reading lists, the author writes that she agrees with those who want students to choose their own books, but not with their arguments. The only good argument for such a choice, in her view, is that choosing what to read teaches young people to judge for themselves. Which of the following could be one of the arguments that the author rejects?
choices: Students who choose their own books gradually learn to decide for themselves which books are worth reading
Students whose teachers chose their books read more classics than students who chose for themselves
Only experienced teachers know which books will develop independent judgment
Students who chose their own books at school tend to go on reading after they leave school
explanation: The argument she rejects must support free choice and differ from her own; (4) is such an argument. (1) is her own argument in other words, and (2) and (3) argue against free choice.

steps.stem: Below is a sentence from which a word or phrase is missing: "____ the long delay, the passengers waited patiently on the platform." In which of the following sentences could the same word or phrase be missing?
choices: ____ the heat wave, many residents spent the weekend at the beach
The festival was canceled ____ the storm
____ the warnings of the weather service, hundreds of hikers set out on the trail
____ the new road that was opened last year, the trip from the city to the village now takes half as long
explanation: The missing phrase is "Despite" (or "In spite of"), which fits only (3). (1) and (2) need "Because of", and (4) needs "Thanks to".

steps.stem:
Shimrit, back from a weekend at the lake, told her friend Orna: "My uncle, who lives near the lake, told me that yesterday he saw Tova rowing with the university team, and that she looked very happy."
Orna replied: "I did not know that your uncle rows on the university team."
Orna apparently understood that -
choices: Shimrit's uncle was one of the rowers
Tova is a member of the university team
Shimrit's uncle was happy to see Tova
Tova rowed on the lake every day that week
explanation: "Rowing with the university team" can describe Tova or the uncle; Orna's reply shows she took it to describe the uncle (1). (2) is what Shimrit meant, and (3) and (4) are not in the sentence.

steps.stem: In the introduction to a collection of letters written by settlers in the Galilee in the early twentieth century, the editor warns readers that the letters were not written for historians. Most were sent to relatives abroad whom the writers wanted to reassure, and they say little about hardship. The letters are therefore an important source, the editor writes, but not a complete picture of life in the settlements. Which of the following is implied in the introduction?
choices: The settlers wrote more letters to their relatives abroad than to one another
The editor believes that letters are not a reliable source for historical research
Most of the settlers who wrote the letters later returned to their countries of origin
Life in the settlements was probably harder than the letters suggest
explanation: The writers played down hardship to reassure their relatives, so life was probably harder than the letters show (4). (1) confuses the letters in the collection with all letters written, (2) contradicts "an important source", and (3) is not mentioned.

steps.stem: After a mathematics exam, several students complained to their teacher that the questions were not like the exercises they had practiced in class. The teacher answered: "Someone who has learned only the way from his house to the grocery store is lost the day the store moves." In his answer, the teacher compares -
choices: the students who complained to people who have never left their own neighborhood
learning only the way to the store to learning only the practiced exercises
the classroom in which the exercises were practiced to the house from which the way begins
the store's move to the students' complaint
explanation: Knowing one fixed route is like knowing only the practiced exercises, and the store's move is like the new questions (2). (4) matches the move to the complaint instead of the exam; (1) and (3) match people and places that play no part in the comparison.

steps.stem: An architect who designed several kibbutz dining halls in the 1950s recalled that the planners had tried to fit each hall to the members' way of life. Within a few years, he said, it was the other way round: where people sat, whom they met and even how the general meetings were run were determined by the layout of the hall. Which of the following best describes the change that the architect noticed?
choices: Buildings that were designed to suit a way of life came to shape that way of life
The halls suited the members in the 1950s, but not the way of life that developed later
The planners ignored the members' way of life when they designed the halls
The members disliked the halls but had no choice but to adapt to them
explanation: The halls were planned to follow the members' life and ended up shaping it (1). (2) reverses the direction of influence, (3) contradicts the planners' effort, and (4) adds dissatisfaction.

steps.stem: A music critic wrote about a certain singer: "Many people believe that her early recordings are weaker than her later ones, and point to the fact that for years hardly anyone bought them. But the public was slow to appreciate them for reasons that had nothing to do with the recordings themselves, and anyone who listens to them today will find them no less moving than her later work." Which of the following best expresses the critic's main point?
choices: The public now prefers the singer's early recordings to her later ones
The singer's later recordings are better, which is why they sold more
Poor sales of the early recordings are no evidence that they are inferior to her later ones
The early recordings sold poorly because of the poor technical conditions in which they were made, unlike the later ones
explanation: The critic rejects the inference from poor sales to lower quality (3). (2) is the view he argues against, (4) gives a reason connected to the recordings themselves, which he denies, and (1) claims a present preference he does not mention.

steps.stem: In a letter to a local newspaper, a resident writes that he voted against moving the market out of the town center, and that he still thinks the decision was taken too hastily. Nevertheless, he admits, the streets of the center have been cleaner since the move - the very thing that the plan's opponents, himself included, had said would not happen. Which of the following is not implied by the letter?
choices: The plan's opponents did not expect the move to make the center cleaner
The resident still has reservations about the way the decision was made
At least one of the opponents' predictions turned out to be wrong
Since the move, the resident has come to support moving the market
explanation: He concedes only that the streets are cleaner and still criticizes the decision, so nothing implies that he now supports the move (4). (1) and (3) follow from "said would not happen", and (2) from "still thinks ... too hastily".

steps.stem: A philosopher once remarked that a man who announces that he is the humblest person in the village has not only praised himself but, by the very announcement, has shown that he does not deserve the praise, whereas a man who announces that he is the proudest person in the village may be telling the truth. Which of the following best expresses the philosopher's point?
choices: Anyone who praises himself is lying
A proud man who openly admits his pride shows by doing so that he is in fact humble
Declaring oneself humble, unlike declaring oneself proud, undermines the very claim being made
A man who is truly humble does not say anything about his own character, whether good or bad
explanation: Announcing one's humility is itself immodest, whereas announcing one's pride can be true (3). (1) contradicts "may be telling the truth", and (2) and (4) are not said.
